Our Git Model Strategy

01 / OUR RECOMMENDATION

Planning a clear publication early

A separate public corpus in a GitHub project organisation contains the released data. The research repo remains responsible for sources, preparation and own studies.

Example and Tip

Example: Before the first workshop are target group, data scope, folder structure, examination and release path in the versioned publication concept.

Tip: A separate publication repository prevents internal working versions from being published casually.

02 / OUR RECOMMENDATION

Offering a significant collection

data/tei contains the book files according to a documented model. README, schema, license, citation and a small example are included.

Example and Tip

Example: A user finds in README: "For analysis, use data/tei of this release. Examples are in examples/.

Tip: Take the structure as a starting point. Own supplements get an explained function.

03 / OUR RECOMMENDATION

Check every change

Changes come via a pull request. Automatic checks run with each proposal; a second person reads the affected bodies professionally against.

Example and Tip

Example: A converter changes ten books: schema and check references, compare inventory changes and read back at least the affected structure types.

Tip: A running script is not a proof of quality. Test scope and editorial approval are recorded.

04 / OUR RECOMMENDATION

Publish Verified Releases

Released stands receive tag, release, change notes and an independent archive package with version proof.

Example and Tip

Example: v1.1 complements collections and corrects solutions. CHANGELOG mentions the changes; v1.0 is retained as a previous state of research.

Tip: Do not overwrite already published versions tacitly. Correct errors in a new version.

05 / OUR RECOMMENDATION

Making local research possible

Full downloads, small entry data, relative paths and documented dependencies are mandatory. An API is an additional offer.

Example and Tip

Example: A newly unpacked example returns the specified result with a documented call – without a university account or network drive.

Tip: Check the entry on another computer. Document the actual tested environment.

06 / OUR RECOMMENDATION

Determine research receipts

Each study refers to data release, selection, extraction and scripting. An analysis manifest combines this information.

Example and Tip

Example: The Reimstudie uses release v1.0, four puzzle identifiers and the designated export without solutions.

Tip: Save the proof together with the examination, not only as a link to the current repo.

07 / OUR RECOMMENDATION

Version new annotation separately

Additional automatic word annotation is first published as a version-off layer. It calls basic release, anchor, procedure and test status.

Example and Tip

Example: A word type annotation refers to v1.0 and the tokenization there. Users can obtain basic data without this layer.

Tip: A technically decided change to the basic model is possible; it receives a new basic release. Additional research remains initially separate.

08 / OUR RECOMMENDATION

Name responsibility after end of project

At least two authorized access routes, a well-kept guide and a reachable contact secure the operation. Limited conservation care applies after the sponsor.

Example and Tip

Example: README mentions who checks important corrections and that new books are recorded after available capacity.

Tip: Try usage and release preparation before leaving the main editor.
